opportunities.name: Benefits email intake triage
opportunities.why_now: The public access plan calls for faster resident response, but the inventory signal is still idea-stage.
opportunities.decision_ask: Assign a Benefits owner and approve a two-week evidence validation sprint.
opportunities.business_problem: Benefits staff manually interpret incoming eligibility emails and route attachments without a documented owner or baseline.
opportunities.agentic_enhancement: Summarize message intent, identify missing information, and recommend a queue while a human approves every route.

controls: Human review before every route update
deployment.notes: Do not select implementation components until deployment and GenAI policy are confirmed.

value_case.label: medium
value_case.basis: Potential response-time and rework improvement; volume and handling time are not available.

opportunities.feasibility: Start read-only with sampled messages after an owner confirms labels and exception boundaries.
opportunities.governance: Treat eligibility content as confidential and require human approval before queue assignment.
validation_questions: Who will own the Benefits email intake pilot?
What message volume and current handling time establish the baseline?

pilot.objective: Measure whether assisted triage improves routing accuracy without autonomous decisions.
pilot.narrow_scope: One Benefits inbox, one message category, and read-only recommendations.
pilot.agent_role: Summarize email intent and recommend a destination queue.
pilot.human_role: Approve every recommendation and label errors for review.
exit_criteria: At least 85 percent routing acceptance with no unauthorized data exposure
pilot.first_step: Name the process owner and approve access to a redacted sample.
